item.content:encoded:
All the way to the end of the comments, and CCKinnison beat me to part of my point.

It is not possible for this to be in Foundation custody.
If the kid was "lucky" enough to be in the exact orbitward spot on the globe when activating, he'd just slam down at too-many-numbers-to-matter mps, destroying the device (unless it is properly impervious to all damage). Otherwise, and this seems to be the case, he'd be dragged laterally through ANYTHING (see below), and eventually fly into space.

My main point is that after each use, the item is destroyed or lost in space (although it could present a K-level event in 365.25 days). Even if we toss out the fun numbers, the core idea as written is flawed.

The other problem is that if this device functions when "on," and not just at the moment it is turned "on," it is far more powerful than people are giving it credit. If it continuously negates inertia (with the sun as a static referent point), then the energy calculations for impacts should not use the mass of the item and attached corpse-smear.

They should use the mass of THE SUN, since that is what this thing is pinned to.

So how much energy did Billy have behind him as he smashed through his home, likely "as the mole tunnels" though the earth's crust and mantle, back out of the crust, and into space?
8.9505x1035 kilojoules.
That's 2.139220841x1017 gigatons!
The annual solar energy output is only 1031 kilojoules!
An activation of this device is a world-ender. If they're lucky and it's activated at an anti-orbitward spot, it still leaves a deadly package in Earth's orbital path. Orbital wobble might save us for a while, but not forever.

If I might offer a pair of fixes:
1. The device functions for an incredibly short span before draining the 8 AA batteries needed (say 1 nanosecond or picosecond). That leaves the subject flying at stupidly lethal speed, but not "pinned to the Sun" when impacting.
2. It took several incidents where the packaging was found to identify the item responsible, and testing has been done with recovered unused SCP-385. Except under unusual circumstances, the objects can only be used once.

item.content:encoded:
Orbital velocity of the planet (I mean, the speed that the Earth is moving in it's orbit, not the speed needed to orbit IT) is ~107,000 kilometers per hour. So setting, even for an instant, the inertial reference frame of an individual to zero with respect to the sun will result in escape velocity… although due to atmospheric drag, the body (dead body) would fall below that speed before actually getting out of the atmosphere.

Basically, I don't see how the belt could have survived the first impact. …One assumes that the belt actually does two things:
1: nullifies all gravitational phenomena for the subject wearing it.
2: Instantaneously (as in, for an instant AND in an instant) "resets" the momentum of the subject with respect to the sun, and ONLY the sun. If inertia REMAINED nullified, the wearer would instantly stop when they touched a wall with zero deceleration (assuming indoor use)… maybe. How an object would behave without inertia is the subject of several interesting pieces of science fiction. (E.E. Smith's Lensman series, and Larry Niven's Gil Hamilton have both dealt with it)

The Factory built it, so it's not surprising that it's deadly. But most of it's products are useful in some twisted way… I don't see a way that this one is, as currently constituted.

…what if it based the new momentum on the Moon, instead of the sun? (does math) If I've done this right, it would give a velocity of ~3500 KM/H… Ballpark of Mach 3. Nope, still not useful or survivable.

…No vote. I mean, it's useful, it's creepy, but WHY did the Factory make it? As written, it's a fancy way to assassinate kids. Possibly with a LOT of property damage, if the subject is on the dawn side of the planet at activation. A 40 KG child (88 pounds) would generate… about 17.5 Gigajoules. or… call it (very roughly) 4.5 Tons of TNT.

item.content:encoded:
After reading through how this SCP developed, I feel it's a little ruined. The initial concept being a flying harness, and the downside being the completely deadly "unintended" consequences of being removed from gravity didn't make PHYSICS sense, but it made NARRATIVE sense. As it's created now, you lose gravitational effects AND have your inertia set to zero (sun relative), with the dire results. While this makes PHYSICS sense, it no longer makes NARRATIVE sense, since it's lost that sinister "be careful what you wish for" feel. Losing inertia is a tacked on secondary effect that kills the subject, but places none of the blame (fairly or not) on the subject for their foolishness in the way I feel this SCP was intended to do.

It's like if you had a Horn of Plenty that made so much food you'd die from eating it, but then people asked "why wouldn't you just stop". So then it was edited so that when used a guy shows up out of nowhere and shoots you in the head. Total loss of ironic demise. (Note to self, new SCP idea…)

You can't really "counteract the influence of inertia" - inertia is not a force acting on an object, but a result of that force. You can set something's inertia to zero for a given frame of reference: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inertial_frame_of_reference

From the sound of this one, the Sun is the frame of reference; the whole Milky Way is moving at an even faster clip, but that would almost assuredly reach escape velocity and fling SCP-385 off the planet entirely.

item.content:encoded:
Finally. I have been reading through this and it bothered me how wrong it was. You would drift slowly away from the planet, not rocket off (where would that energy come from?)

Think of it like your on the outside of some massive space ship, going a constant speed, with magnetic boots. You turn your boots off. You don't rocket away from the ship, you keep going the same as you were before. There is no change in your vector in relation to the ships.

Now if the ship were spinning while orbiting (like the earth around the sun) you would continue in a straight line parallel with the surface that you were on (think of string hanging off the surface of a ball.) Those who witnessed this would see you floating off slowly at a diagonal. You would be moving the same speed (minus air drag) and direction while the body you were on slowly continued spinning (slowly in relation to your speed, anyway.)

From a physics forum posing the same question:

 Well, we (the people) move on rotating Earth with very SMALL acceleration a = w2R = 0.034 m/sec2, so upon turning gravity "off" we just start slowly rizing up (with this acceleration). In 1 sec we will be 1.7 cm above Earth, in 10 sec - 1.7 m above Earth, in 1 min - 60 m above, in 10 min - 6 km and so on. Well, better to say that Earth will be that far down (we will move straight, but Earth will continue to rotate, thus to slowly move down for us). And this is on equator. On poles no motion away from Earth takes place at all.

Physics Forum Post

item.content:encoded:
We must all remember the (paraphrased) words of Sir Isaac Newton: "Every action has an equal and opposite reaction."

Under normal circumstances, an object at rest is applying a downward force upon the planet, and the planet is pushing back equally well, hence why we don't just sink into the ground (usually). Gravity is what's currently holding us down on the ground.

Take gravity out of the equation, and you may not INSTANTLY shoot through the air like a quantum rocket, but you *will* be airborne going at something like 1 m/s give or take, and if standing still going pretty much straight up at first. If you're inside, it's unlikely you'll be insta-gibbed, but you're probably gonna get a bad headache from slamming into the ceiling, then every other surface as you keep bouncing around until you grab onto something solid. If you're outside, well, unless you're standing under a tree or powerline, you'll have a nice view of the clouds before you start suffocating.

All that said, I'd love to see someone have one of these things and try to use it as a parachute without realizing it DOESN'T cancel current momentum, and keep frantically hitting the button wondering why they're not slowing down. The sadist in me would laugh.

item.content:encoded:
The idea of instant splats is not without merit, that would be the the danger inherent if the device had canceled your momentum in addition to gravity's influence.

But just to put this issue to rest I'm probably going to start working on an update note for clarification. It's not the power of centrifugal force that gets you itself — it's that the planet is going tens of thousands of miles per hour in one direction while you are going tens of thousands of miles per hour in a different direction. That ends in a collision or what appears to be a launch into orbit space from the perspective of others.

Anti-gravity is often used to describe a force that is pushing against the Earth's pull while still leaving you as part of the larger system. In that sense of the term, the Earth's spin and orbit aren't much of a big deal because gravity is still there. That's not what this device does, and that is a fatal distinction.

in case anyone wasnt sure on this article(which it sounds like from earlier comments), removing all gravitational effects is all this needs to do to produce these results. dont go thinking it's stopping you dead in place. if this somehow fixed your position in space, then for one you'd be the only object in the universe whose position and speed wasn't relative, people could use you as an absolute :P that part would be fun

but it would also mean an instant "acceleration" to, at minimum, 100,000 kph relative to the earth's position, which would blow you straight through basically anything in your path on your rather rapid departure. this also would happen if, rather than fixing your position in space, it just completely stopped your momentum vs the earth's motion. this article doesnt describe that kind of effect….

if gravity ceased to affect you then your trajectory would be whatever straight-line direction the earth had been moving you in, acceleration rapid but not instantaneous. it might be a "gradual" shift for the first half second or so, but it would become a major deal very very quickly. you might survive if you were very close to a wall as you wouldnt have enough time to build up much speed before you slammed into it, but you'd be pinned quite firmly by centrifugal force.

i'm curious about the math on that as to what angle/speed you would start moving in, but do agree this is about what you could expect as your result. just hope that it doesnt get activated outside.
